title: Split tenant write path to append-only event log with background compaction
creator: Nina Kaur
description: Problem: Frequent small updates to tenant_event and tenant_metadata tables cause high write amplification, lock contention on hot partitions, and bloat in MVCC leading to long-tail read latencies during rollouts. Goal: Introduce an append-only event log as the primary write path for tenant-scoped updates, plus an async compaction/merge pipeline that produces read-optimized projections. This reduces write amplification, simplifies transactional patterns, and enables safer online migrations. Success criteria: 40-60% reduction in write IOPS on control-plane primary instances under synthetic replay workload; 30% reduction in tail p99 read latency for cross-tenant queries; no more than 5% increase in end-to-end tail latency for writes during rollout; migration can be rolled back without data loss within 24 hours.
non_goals: Full denormalization of all control-plane tables in this cycle
Replacing existing OLAP reporting pipelines (separate project)
motivation_and_tradeoffs: Append-only design minimizes locks and leverages sequential writes for better throughput on NVMe/PMEM-backed instances.
Tradeoff: introduces eventual consistency for read projections; mitigated by configurable sync points and short TTLs for critical keys.
Tradeoff: extra storage overhead during rollout due to dual-writes for cutover window; acceptable given expected reduction in snapshot churn.
Prefer background compaction vs synchronous merge to maintain write tail latency SLOs.
Will keep existing schema read paths intact behind feature flag until projection parity verified.
migration_plan: 1) Add new table tenant_event_log (append-only, partitioned by tenant_id) and migration-safe schemas in a non-blocking migration.
2) Implement service-level write adapter: writes go to tenant_event_log and continue to write to existing tables under feature-flagged dual-write for validation.
3) Deploy background compactor that consumes log, performs idempotent compaction into projection table tenant_projection_v2.
4) Enable read routing for low-risk routes to tenant_projection_v2 behind feature flag and run A/B traffic (5-25%).
5) Gradually increase read traffic to 100% after correctness and performance verification, then deprecate legacy read paths and retire dual-write after 1 week of stability.
6) Backfill missing historical state using offline replay job for tenants that need immediate parity.
7) Finalize schema cleanup: drop redundant columns/indexes from legacy tables and introduce partial-indexes on projection table optimized for common filters.
rollback_plan: If projection parity or performance regressions occur:
- Flip feature flag to route reads back to legacy tables (no writes lost because log is authoritative).
- Pause compactor; keep log intact for forensic replay.
- Re-enable dual-write (if previously disabled) to ensure any writes during cutover are present in legacy tables.
- Revert schema drops using phased DDLs that add columns back (online-safe).
risks: Compactor bugs could produce incorrect projections: mitigated with idempotency checks and replay tests.
Increased storage costs during rollout from dual-write: tracked and capped in rollout plan.
Edge-case transactional semantics for multi-row tenant updates may need small synchronous verification windows.
Long-running backfill could impact IO; plan includes rate-limits and a low-priority maintenance window.
Rollback complexity if legacy schema already pruned by other parallel migrations (coordinate with ENG-41205 and ENG-27358).
test_plan: Unit tests for write adapter and compactor idempotency.
Integration test: end-to-end write->compactor->projection correctness with random interleaved updates.
Staging soak: 72h with 25% production traffic replay and chaos injection (leader failover, high IO).
Performance benchmark: synthetic tenant replay to measure write IOPS and p99 read tail before/after change.
Migration canary: roll out to single non-critical region and validate metrics/dashboards for 48h before global ramp.
observability_and_metrics: New metrics: tenant_event_log_write_ios, compactor_lag_seconds, compactor_processed_events_total, projection_apply_errors_total.
Dashboards: write IOPS heatmap, compactor lag vs. projection discrepancy count, long-tail read latency by tenant.
SLOs: compactor lag < 60s for 99% tenants within 30 days of rollout; projection_apply_errors_total == 0 after parity verification.
Alerting: compactor_lag_seconds > 300s for >5% tenants triggers P1 alert.
